key_insight: A machine learning architecture learns holographic quantum circuit syntax and parameters to extrapolate toward longer or more expressive circuits.
engineering_relevance: Reusing measured and reset qubits enables sampling from large quantum states with fixed qubit resources, while additional persistent ancillas exponentially increase effective bond dimension.
method: Use physical qubits with mid-circuit measurements and resets, coupled to persistent ancillas.
Learn gate, measurement, and reset sequences alongside rotation parameters from circuit datasets.
Extrapolate learned syntax and parameters to scale circuit length or expressivity.
evidence_signal: The methodology is demonstrated on an analytically solvable dataset based on a vector-valued generalization of the W-state; the abstract reports no quantitative performance metrics.
watch_item: Generalization beyond the solvable dataset and robustness to hardware noise remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: A machine learning architecture for scaling of holographic quantum circuits
